record.original_question: Let F1 , F2 be Finsler metrics on a closed surface of genus ≥ 2.

evidence.quote: Let F1 , F2 be Finsler metrics on a closed surface of genus ≥ 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Two Finsler metrics $F_1, F_2$ on a smooth manifold $M$ are called projectively equivalent if every unparametrized oriented geodesic of $F_1$ is an unparametrized oriented geodesic of $F_2$ (and vice versa). Note that for any Finsler metric $F$ and any closed 1-form $\omega$ on $M$ such that $F + \omega$ is again a (positive) Finsler metric, the metrics $F$ and $F + \omega$ have the same oriented geodesics; the same holds for $F$ and $cF$ with $c > 0$.

Let $\Sigma$ be a closed orientable surface of genus $\geq 2$, and let $F_1, F_2$ be two (smooth) Finsler metrics on $\Sigma$ that are projectively equivalent. Prove or disprove: there must exist a constant $c > 0$ and a closed 1-form $\omega$ on $\Sigma$ such that
$$F_1 = c\, F_2 + \omega.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a conjecture of Matveev. In the real-analytic category, it has been proved: any two real-analytic Finsler metrics on a closed surface of negative Euler characteristic with the same unparametrized oriented geodesics differ by a positive scaling constant and the addition of a closed 1-form (Matveev, "Projectively equivalent Finsler metrics on surfaces of negative Euler characteristic," arXiv:1908.02701, 2019). The general smooth case does not appear to be settled.

status_evidence.title: Projectively equivalent Finsler metrics on surfaces of negative Euler characteristic
status_evidence.snippet: On a surface of negative Euler characteristic, two real-analytic Finsler metrics have the same unparametrized oriented geodesics, if and only if they differ by a scaling constant and addition of a closed 1-form.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is established in the real-analytic case on closed surfaces of genus >= 2.

status_evidence.title: Open problems and questions about geodesics (Burns–Matveev)
status_evidence.snippet: Let F1, F2 be Finsler metrics on a closed surface of genus >= 2. Assume every F1-geodesic is an F2-geodesic. Must F1 = c F2 + closed form?
status_evidence.claim: Source of the projective-equivalence question for Finsler metrics on higher-genus surfaces.
